name: Build once, verify, reuse
summary: A proven query gap may produce a reusable capability; unsupported data is not fixed by inventing a query.

steps.label: Decide whether a query is missing
steps.human:
Select the bounded build outcome only when source data is supported and no offered query fits. Do not write the request.

I/O boundary: Existing fit/choice transports are shown as reusable primitives. This target orchestration remains a specification; selected build is not admission authority.

Example boundary: Only supported source data and an eligible catalog gap offer build; this example chooses build. Separate scope/activation permission remains required.

steps.label: Construct the scoped request
steps.human:
Assemble original need, input/output requirements and source-fit evidence; deduplicate equivalent active builds and dispatch the coding agent. A data gap is not a query build.

I/O boundary: The actual existing QueryBuildRequest is reusable here. Equivalence deduplication and richer target input/output semantics are not claimed as implemented by this payload.

steps.label: Resume the original need
steps.human:
Execute the accepted query for the waiting question, then return to shared attempt comparison. Later requests can reuse the registered version rather than rebuilding it.

Return the executed result to [the shared attempt comparison loop](docs/product-truth/flows/leafcutter/retrieve-project-knowledge.flow.json#compare), which compares attempts before advisory recording, combination and final sufficiency.

This step is reachable only with a verified admitted version. A rejected or failed candidate exits through the failure branch without execution.

Return this attempt and its limits to [shared attempt comparison](docs/product-truth/flows/leafcutter/retrieve-project-knowledge.flow.json#compare) alongside prior or complementary methods. The main route owns comparison, advisory recording and combination once.

I/O boundary: Existing per-operation retrieval result is reusable after actual verified admission.

Example boundary: The admitted example operation and executed result both name example_ac_requirements version 1. This remains an illustrative handoff, not actual activation proof.

branches.label: Stop a rejected build
branches.human:
Do not register or execute the rejected candidate. Preserve its failure, original need and prior evidence; return to [method selection](docs/product-truth/flows/leafcutter/retrieve-project-knowledge.flow.json#plan) for a permitted alternative when useful work/budget remains, otherwise report partial or blocked.

I/O boundary: Existing failed/blocked capability results retain an admission failure without execution; the proposed return to method selection still needs its own binding.

Example boundary: This follows QueryActivationExecutor._failure: status failed with invalid_candidate (or permission_denied for unavailable/mismatched catalog), not retrieval_not_needed.

provenance.note:
Target design — not a delivery claim
User-requested question-first design. This flow is spec/draft; existing runtime and test evidence do not establish this full contract. Existing acceptance criteria are context pending behavioral mapping, not new completion proof.

Traversal and multiple-method design extension
Added bounded method selection/return routes and a shared attempt-comparison handoff. Target specification only; no runtime or acceptance-status change.

Added source-bound field/type/requiredness/default metadata and explicitly illustrative JSON projections. Preserved topology, actor ownership, realization and AC status. Non-JSON artifacts and genuinely undefined proposed interfaces remain explicit.
